risks.title: Competitive pressure from neobanks and BigTech on retail deposits
risks.summary: ING faces increased competition from neobanks (Revolut, N26, Bunq) and technology platforms (Apple Pay, Google) capturing market share in deposits, payments and consumer credit, threatening retail margins in its core markets (Netherlands, Germany, Belgium).
risks.score_rationale: Risk placed at the top of strategic sections in ING's annual report; intensive language ('significant competitive pressure', 'disruptive entrants'). Upward trend with the rise of Revolut, N26 and GAFA entry into payments. Competition category weighs heavily for a pan-European retail bank.

risks.title: AML/KYC regulatory compliance and sanctions risk
risks.summary: ING is subject to strict anti-money laundering (AML) and know your customer (KYC) requirements in over 40 countries. The precedent of the EUR 775 M fine in 2018 and ongoing investigations in several jurisdictions expose the group to additional financial penalties, activity restrictions and lasting reputational damage.
risks.score_rationale: ING paid EUR 775 M in 2018 as part of an AML settlement in the Netherlands; the risk remains mentioned as a priority in each subsequent annual report with strong language ('material risk', 'ongoing regulatory scrutiny'). Stable trend but maximum severity level given the history. Regulation category is the heaviest for European banks.

risks.title: Cyber risk and operational resilience of banking systems
risks.summary: As a predominantly digital bank (ING app, 40+ million online customers), ING is a prime target for cyberattacks (ransomware, DDoS, fraud). Incidents on its platforms could result in service interruptions, direct financial losses and penalties under DORA (Digital Operational Resilience Act) which came into force in January 2025.
risks.score_rationale: Systematically mentioned in the top 5 operational risks of ING's annual report; explicit language ('increasing sophistication of cyber attacks', 'critical infrastructure'). Upward trend with multiplication of sector incidents (DDoS on ING NL in 2023). Cybersecurity category rising sharply for digital banks.

risks.title: Digital transformation and dependency on third-party technology providers
risks.summary: ING depends on cloud providers (AWS, Microsoft Azure) and critical IT service providers for its banking operations. A failure or contractual breach with these partners, or an incident at a subcontractor, could disrupt customer services and expose ING to regulatory non-compliance risks (EBA continuity requirements).
risks.score_rationale: Technology concentration risk mentioned in operational risks section; moderate language ('third-party dependency', 'cloud migration risks'). Upward trend with acceleration of the Think Forward/Accelerate program. Technology category weight growing for banks in transformation.

risks.title: Geopolitical exposure in emerging markets (Turkey, Russia)
risks.summary: ING holds exposures in geopolitically sensitive markets (Turkey via ING Bank A.Ş., former presence in Russia). International sanctions, political instability and currency devaluations (Turkish lira) can generate significant credit losses and force asset disposals at a loss, as observed during the Russia-Ukraine conflict.
risks.score_rationale: Geopolitical risk explicitly addressed in annual report following the Ukraine war and sanctions against Russia; strong language ('material exposure', 'sanctions compliance'). ING had to provision significant losses on its Russian portfolio in 2022-2023. Stable trend after partial divestment but residual risk.

risks.title: Risk of non-compliance with CRR3/Basel IV capital requirements
risks.summary: The entry into force of CRR3/Basel IV imposes a progressive output floor on ING's internal models, likely to significantly increase its risk-weighted assets (RWA) and reduce its CET1 ratio. This could constrain dividend and share buyback policies, or require a capital increase.
risks.score_rationale: CRR3 (Basel IV transposition) comes into force in 2025 with output floor at 72.5%; ING explicitly mentions the impact on its RWA in investor communications. Precise language ('significant increase in risk-weighted assets', 'capital planning uncertainty'). Upward trend with constrained regulatory timeline.

risks.title: Litigation risk and multi-jurisdictional regulatory disputes
risks.summary: ING is exposed to litigation in multiple jurisdictions, including regulatory investigations into AML practices, disputes related to mortgage products (variable rates in the Netherlands) and class actions by customers. These proceedings can result in fines, significant provisions and substantial mobilization of legal and managerial resources.
risks.score_rationale: ING is subject to proceedings in several countries (AML investigations in Italy, Australia, mortgage disputes in the Netherlands); mentioned in notes to financial statements with provisions set aside. Moderate but recurring language. Stable trend with risk of new proceedings.

risks.title: Climate risk and transition to sustainable finance (EU taxonomy)
risks.summary: ING is exposed to climate transition risk through its loan portfolio to carbon-intensive sectors (energy, real estate, transport). Tightening of the EU green taxonomy and CSRD/SFDR requirements may force impairments on stranded assets, while creating competitive pressure to finance the energy transition of its corporate clients.
risks.score_rationale: ING has committed to carbon neutrality of its loan portfolio (Terra approach); the EU taxonomy and CSRD impose increasing reporting obligations. Progressively stronger language ('stranded assets', 'transition risk in lending portfolio'). Upward trend with tightening ESG regulation.

events.title: Voya Financial's (NYSE:VOYA) Q1 CY2026: Strong Sales
events.body: Financial services company Voya Financial (NYSE:VOYA) announced better-than-expected revenue in Q1 CY2026, with sales up 7.6% year on year to $2.03 billion. Its non-GAAP profit of $2.26 per share was 12.8% above analysts' consensus estimate
